quickAnswer: Drive 45 to 55 minutes southwest of central Marmaris and the high-rise resort strip disappears completely, replaced by the quiet coves of Selimiye, Bozburun, and Söğüt. This peninsula is famous for traditional wooden gulet shipyards, pier-side Aegean fish restaurants, and low-rise boutique stays best explored with a rental car.

body.text: Most international visitors hear "Marmaris" and picture neon bar streets, cruise piers, and multi-storey package hotels. That is central Marmaris town—not the rugged peninsula stretching southwest toward the Greek island of Symi. This bozburun selimiye guide shows why seasoned Türkiye travellers drive straight past town to base themselves in the sheltered bays beyond Hisarönü.
Why do seasoned travellers skip central Marmaris for Selimiye and Bozburun?

Central Marmaris caters heavily to high-volume summer package tourism, whereas Selimiye, Bozburun, and neighbouring Söğüt enforce strict low-rise building limits, ban large all-inclusive resorts, and run on a slow maritime rhythm. You trade crowded beach clubs and late-night discos for flat-calm swimming decks, pine-clad hills, and small family-run guesthouses.

Because the Bozburun Peninsula sits inside a Special Environmental Protection Area, you will not find concrete mega-hotels or jet-ski noise slicing across Selimiye Bay. The water stays glassy well into late morning, making it a favourite anchorage for Turkish sailors escaping Bodrum's prices and crowds. Note the honest trade-off: neither Selimiye nor Bozburun has wide golden sand beaches. Swimming happens off wooden hotel piers, stone jetties, or small pebble coves—and by boat in neighbouring bays like Dirsekbükü and Bozukkale.
What makes Bozburun famous for wooden gulet building?

Bozburun is one of Türkiye's last active hubs for handcrafted wooden [Turkish gulets](https://goturkiye.com/tr/bluevoyage/turk-guletleri), where master shipwrights still frame 18- to 35-metre timber hulls by eye and traditional lofting methods. While Bodrum's yards shifted heavily toward refits and superyachts, Bozburun's boatyards continue building and winter-maintaining classic Blue Voyage vessels.

Historically, southwestern Anatolian boatbuilders shaped wide-beamed timber workboats (tırhandil and early fishing gulets) for sponge diving and coastal freight before adapting them for Blue Cruises in the 1960s and 1970s, as documented in [Istanbul Technical University maritime hull research](https://www.az.itu.edu.tr/jfa/article/download/908/695/11658). Today, Bozburun's shipyards sit just west of the harbour road. Between October and April, you can watch timber ribs being planked in pine, mahogany, and iroko; in summer, the finished boats anchor right off Bozburun and Selimiye waiting for charter guests.
Where are the best waterfront fish restaurants?

The peninsula's standout dining happens on narrow wooden piers literally over the sea—ordering chilled olive-oil meze, grilled octopus, and line-caught grouper (lagos) or red mullet (barbun). In Selimiye, Sardunya and Hidayet'in Yeri anchor the waterfront; in Bozburun, Bozburun Yacht Club leads for sunset dining, while nearby Söğüt offers quieter, better-value tables.
A few practical local notes before you book:

items: [Bozburun Yacht Club Restaurant](https://bozburunyachtclub.com/bozburun-restaurant): Reached by road or yacht mooring, serving refined Aegean meze and fresh line-caught fish overlooking the islands—reserve ahead for sunset tables.

[Hidayet'in Yeri (Selimiye)](https://www.hidayetinyeri.com.tr/) & Sardunya Restaurant: Selimiye's two best-known pier institutions. Food is fresh, but summer prices in Selimiye now rival Bodrum—always ask the per-kilogram fish price before ordering, and confirm pier seating when booking.
Söğüt Village (15 minutes south of Bozburun): Less polished and noticeably better value than Selimiye's main strip, with simple seaside family kitchens specializing in octopus and calamari.

body.text: Do you need a car to explore the peninsula?

Yes—unless you plan to stay anchored on a private gulet or never leave your hotel's swimming pier, a rental car is essential on the Bozburun Peninsula. Public dolmuş minibuses run along the main Marmaris–Selimiye–Bozburun spine, but they stop running early in the evening and rarely connect side coves like Söğüt, Turgut, or Bayır smoothly.

Roads across the peninsula are fully paved, well-signed, and scenic, though narrow and winding through pine passes—drive patiently around blind bends and watch for wandering goats. From Dalaman Airport (DLM), expect a 2-hour-15-minute to 2-hour-30-minute drive (roughly 140 km). For arrival logistics, see our [Dalaman vs Antalya Airport guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/dalaman-vs-antalya-airport) or pair this stay with two nights on the river via our [Dalyan and İztuzu guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/dalyan-iztuzu-guide).

faq.q: Which airport is closest to Selimiye and Bozburun?
faq.a: Dalaman Airport (DLM) is the closest gateway, roughly 135 to 145 kilometres away (about 2 hours 15 minutes to 2 hours 30 minutes by car via Marmaris). Milas–Bodrum Airport (BJV) takes slightly longer unless you time the Bodrum–Datça car ferry.

faq.q: Are Selimiye and Bozburun good for families with young children?
faq.a: They suit older children who swim confidently off deep-water piers. Families with toddlers who need shallow sandy beaches often prefer Dalyan's İztuzu Beach, Ölüdeniz, or a Belek resort instead.

faq.q: When is the best time of year to visit the Bozburun Peninsula?
faq.a: Late May, June, September, and early October deliver warm sea temperatures (23–26°C), open restaurants, and far calmer mooring bays than peak July–August, when Turkish holiday traffic fills Selimiye's narrow waterfront road.

faq.q: Can you take a day boat trip from Selimiye or Bozburun without chartering a full week?
faq.a: Yes. Both harbours have licensed daily wooden boats offering private or small-group full-day swims to Bencik Bay, Kamelya Island, Dişlice Island, and Dirsekbükü—far quieter than Marmaris's loud party boats.

faq.q: Is Bozburun worth visiting in winter?
faq.a: Most boutique hotels, yacht-club restaurants, and seasonal pier cafes close between November and mid-April. Winter suits travellers specifically interested in quiet hiking and watching wooden gulet construction in the boatyards, not swimming or dining variety.

faq.q: Can you visit the Greek island of Symi from Bozburun?
faq.a: Fast passenger ferries to Symi operate seasonally from central Marmaris harbour (about 50 minutes away) and Datça, not directly from Bozburun's village quay. Check Schengen visa rules and ferry schedules in advance.
